title: Grateful Dead Live at Boston Music Hall on 1971-04-08

ai_review.summary: Mostly clean soundboard with occasional noise/dropouts, yet captures a blistering April ’71 set highlighted by a smoking Dark Star → St. Stephen → NFA and fiery China > Rider.
ai_review.review: The performance is widely praised for its high energy and strong song selection – standout moments include the concise Dark Star into St. Stephen and NFA, the debut of Second That Emotion, a hot China‑Rider segue with Pigpen on Wurlitzer, and a soaring Good Lovin' encore.  The soundboard source is generally clear but suffers from noticeable noise, volume drops and occasional low‑end loss, making it a fair‑to‑good listening experience after some cleanup.

ai_rating.rationale: Most reviewers give 4–5 stars and highlight exceptional musical moments; recording flaws are noted but do not dominate, resulting in an overall strong rating.

recording_quality.technical_notes: Frequent noise, volume drop‑outs, low‑end loss and occasional glitches (especially on Loser, Second That Emotion, Dark Star), but overall a mostly clean SBD with decent clarity after editing.

standout_songs: Dark Star > St. Stephen > Not Fade Away
show_quality.setlist_flow: Spring ’71 setlist flows well with a strong first set and an even more explosive second set; the Dark Star opens set two and leads into classic jams, while the closing Good Lovin' provides a high‑octane finish.

band_member_comments.Jerry: Hot leads throughout, soaring wah‑wah on Good Lovin', tasty noodling in Dark Star; generally praised for strong guitar work.
band_member_comments.Phil: Unusual and powerful bass lines noted especially during the Dark Star and Second That Emotion debut.
band_member_comments.Bob: Terrific solo on Rider and strong vocal contributions; highlighted as a highlight of the China>Rider segue.
band_member_comments.Keys: Pigpen on electric Wurlitzer piano during China, Ned Lagin providing ghostly fills and spacey textures in jams.
